To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the eight individual models of technology acceptance explain between 17 percent (theory of reasoned action) and 53 percent (theory of planned behavior) of the variance in intention to use new technology, (2) a unified model of user acceptance, UTAUT, was formulated, and (3) UTAUT outperforms the eight individual models and provides a useful tool to managers needing to assess new technology introductions.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the determinants of user acceptance of information systems.
understanding the determinants of user intentions to use and actual use of new technology in organizations and the moderators of these relationships.
the question of why people adopt and use information technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Unified Theory of Technology Acceptance and Use (UTAUT) is a useful tool for understanding and predicting user acceptance of information technology.
UTAUT is a good model of technology acceptance and use.
UTAUT is a useful tool for assessing the likelihood of success of new technology introductions, as well as understanding the drivers of acceptance and designing interventions to promote acceptance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UTAUT provides an integrative and generalizable model of user acceptance of information technology.
the unified theory is a useful tool for predicting user acceptance and usage of new information systems.
UTAUT is a parsimonious model that explains 70% of variance in technology acceptance and use and is thus an important contribution to our understanding of technology use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field is moving towards a more unified view of acceptance and use of technology.
a unified view of acceptance can provide a useful tool for both researchers and managers.
there are four key determinants of technology use and acceptance that can be targeted by managers to improve the success of technology introductions.
